youtube.title: Halves and Quarters for Kids! Fair Shares Picnic | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
One last sandwich and two hungry friends! Robo's magic cutting line and the Unfair Cut Alarm teach fair shares: equal parts, halves and quarters (fourths), two ways to cut a square, a round pizza in quarters, and why a half is bigger than a quarter.
For first graders learning equal parts. Fold paper squares into halves and quarters at home; grown-ups do any cutting.

do.text: A sunny picnic! And one last sandwich.
Mine!
No, mine!
Wait! One sandwich and two friends. How can we make it fair?
Easy! Give it all to me!
Ha ha! Nice try, Frog.
Our mission: share fairly. I'm not hungry. I ate a battery sandwich!
Fair shares are equal parts. Equal means the same size.
equal
Here is my magic cutting line. No knives!
I'm bigger!
I'm smaller!
Uh-oh. The Unfair Cut Alarm! The parts are not equal.
not equal
How can I fix it? Where should I cut?
Right through the middle!
Ding! The two parts are the same size. Fair!
fair
Two equal parts are called halves.
halves
Same and same is fair, fair, fair!
Halves two ways! First, cut straight down.
Two rectangles. Two halves!
Now another way. Corner to corner!
Two triangles. They are halves too!
halves
Both ways are fair!
Now the long cake bar. Cut it in half.
Two squares. Each one is half the cake.
halves
Here's a real trick for sharing with a friend.
One friend cuts. The other friend chooses first.
I'll cut! I'll make it very fair.
I choose this one. That's fair!
Fun fact: one cuts, one chooses is a very old trick.
Now four friends share one sandwich.
Robo, Frog, Bunny and Bear. 1, 2, 3, 4!
Cut in half. Then in half again!
Four equal parts are called quarters.
quarters
Quarters are also called fourths.
fourths
Fun fact: quarter and fourth mean the same thing!
Another way. Corner to corner, two times!
Four triangles. Four quarters!
quarters
And the round pizza.
One cut makes halves.
halves
Two cuts make quarters!
quarters
Four the same, that's quarters! Same and same is fair!
Let's test the Unfair Cut Alarm. Fair or not fair?
fair or not fair
Thumbs up for fair. Wobble your hands for not fair!
Cut one.
Not fair! One part is bigger.
not fair
Cut two. The pizza in four parts.
Fair! Four equal parts. Quarters!
fair
Cut three. The cake bar in three parts.
Not fair! Three parts, and they are not equal.
not equal
Not halves, not quarters. Great checking!

scenes.title: Half or quarter: which is bigger?

do.text: Robo, can I please have the bigger half?
Let's look. Two equal sandwiches.
This one is in halves. That one is in quarters.
Which is bigger, a half or a quarter?
One half covers two quarters exactly!
one half covers two quarters
More parts means smaller parts. A half is bigger.
a half is bigger
And look at our two halves, Frog.
Wait... they're the same! There's no bigger half!
That's right! When it's fair, halves are the same.
Fair shares quiz! Think, then shout.
Fair Shares Quiz
Question one. One big part and one small part. Halves?
No! The parts are not equal. Not halves.
Question two. How many quarters make one whole?
4 quarters! 1, 2, 3, 4.
Question three. Which is bigger, a half or a quarter?
A half! A half is two quarters.
Question four. Bunny and Bear share one cake bar.
How many equal parts? What are they called?
2 equal parts, called halves!
halves
Last one. A circle in 4 equal parts. What is each part?
A quarter! Also called a fourth.
quarter, fourth
Five out of five!
Picnic time! One sandwich, four fair quarters.
Yum! Beep beep! A battery sandwich quarter.
Try it at home! Fold a paper square in half.
Do the edges match? Then fold it in half again.
Open it up. Four quarters! Grown-ups do any cutting.
Equal parts are fair. Two equal parts are halves.
Four equal parts are quarters!
Same, same, fair game! Bye, friends!
